title: Temporal Roles Dashboard and Appeals Flow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: As Redwood expands Private and Dedicated offerings, customers are asking for more granular, time-bounded access controls and clearer audit trails for temporary role grants. This ticket designs a console-first experience that combines a Temporal Roles Dashboard (overview of active, scheduled, and historical time-limited grants) with an Appeals Flow for users to request retroactive access reviews and owners to approve/deny. Goals: 1) Surface temporal role state across orgs/workspaces so admins can quickly find active escalations; 2) Make audit trails easy to consume and linkable (deep links to request IDs, operators, and evidence); 3) Provide a lightweight self-serve appeals request flow for users who believe a denied access or missing permission caused a production impact; 4) Minimize friction for reviewers while maintaining auditability for compliance. Constraints: must reuse console role model (no backend schema changes assumed for initial MVP), align with RBAC audit logs exportability, work within existing Console nav patterns. Deliverables: Figma prototype covering dashboard, grant detail panel, appeals request modal, reviewer queue; clickthrough scenarios for common workflows; annotated spec for engineering (API surface, telemetry events, SLO considerations).
acceptance_criteria: Design files (Figma) include Temporal Roles Dashboard with filters (workspace, role, status, time window) and a grant-detail flyout with event timeline
Appeals flow prototype allows user to submit request with attached evidence, links to relevant audit log entries, and selects reviewer(s)
Reviewer queue shows pending appeals with quick-approve/deny, comment, and escalate options; actions generate structured events that can be consumed by console backend
All screens include deep-linkable IDs and copy for compliance export (CSV/JSON), and a handoff spec enumerating telemetry keys and required API endpoints
Usability review completed with at least 3 PM/Eng/Security stakeholders and documented follow-ups

notes_for_engineering: See attached handoff PDF for telemetry keys. Proposed lightweight API: GET /v1/audit/temporal-grants?workspace_id=...; POST /v1/appeals {requester, grant_id, evidence[]}. Engineering to confirm payload shape. Telemetry: appeals.submitted, appeals.reviewed, temporal_grant.expired, temporal_grant.revoked. Include deep link token in response for reproducible audit exports.
ux_decisions: 1) Default dashboard view shows active grants only; historical grants hidden behind a time-range toggle to reduce noise. 2) Single-click deep link copies grant ID URL for incident docs. 3) Appeals are treated as first-class console objects with their own lifecycle so auditors can query them separately. 4) Reviewer fast-path supports canned responses but requires custom justification for denials. 5) Exports include both human-readable timeline and raw event IDs for downstream compliance tools.
